newsitem.title: USA: Bausch & Lomb profits dip, announces restructuring.
newsitem.headline: Bausch & Lomb profits dip, announces restructuring.

text.p: Bausch & Lomb, a major maker of eye care products, announced Wednesday a plunge in quarterly earnings and said it will spend an estimated $80 million on a major restructuring over 1997 and 1998.
The company said it will reinvest annual savings of $100 million by 1999 to ensure long-term growth and provide a more predictable economic return for its investors.
Bausch & Lomb's profits dipped to $3.3 million, or 6 cents a share, in the three months ended March 29 from $22.5 million, or 39 cents a share, in the year-ago period.
Sales fell to $451.2 million from $469.3 million as a stronger dollar reduced foreign revenues. On a constant dollar basis, Bausch & Lomb said its revenues from ongoing operations rose 3 percent.
The results exclude $14.9 million in revenues in the 1996 first quarter from the company's oral care and dental implant businesses, which were divested in the latter half of the year.

The company took a $12.8 million pre-tax charge in the quarter, and expects to recognise about $55 million to $60 million in restructuring costs by the end of 1997, most of which are expected to be recorded in the second quarter.

Bausch & Lomb also made a provision of $6.8 million after taxes for the expected cost of discontinuing certain sunglass product lines, and for writing-off the company's equity stake in a start-up technology venture.

The discontinued products, Ray-Ban speciality sunglasses for driving and performance sports, compete in niche segments which the company said it believes can be reached more effectively through other brands.

The restructuring is expected to result in improved operating margins, particularly in the company's eyewear business. The remainder of the savings will come from restructuring administrative functions, Bausch said.

The Rochester, N.Y.-based company said the savings generated are on top of annual savings of $50 million that the company had identified through projects announced in early 1996. The company said that these existing plans are on track.

Bausch & Lomb said it plans to phase out sunglass component manufacturing at its Frame Centre in Rochester and to "optimize" manufacturing operations in the sunglass global product delivery centres in San Antonio, Texas, Waterford, Ireland, and Hong Kong.

Bausch & Lomb's core businesses include soft and rigid gas permeable contact lenses, lens care products, premium sunglasses and ophthalmic pharmaceutical products. Its brands include Bausch & Lomb, Arnette, Curel, SofLens66, Boston, Killer Loop and ReNu. The company has more than 13,000 employees in 35 countries.
Bausch & Lomb's stock added 37.5 cents to $39.50 in early trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
